'''Thomas Joseph Katz''' (born March 21, 1936) is an American organic chemist known for his experimental work with [[prismane]], [[olefin metathesis]], and [[enyne metathesis]]. He is an emeritus professor at [[Columbia University]].

== Early life and education ==
Thomas Joseph Katz was born on March 21, 1936, in [[Prague]], then Czechoslovakia, from which his family escaped to Canada after the Nazi invasion in March 1939.   His family settled for three years in [[Toronto]], Canada, and then moved to New York City, where Katz attended public schools.

Katz graduated from the University of Wisconsin in 1956 and then went, under an [[NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program]], to [[Harvard University]] for studies in chemistry and research in [[Robert Burns Woodward|R. B. Woodward]]’s laboratory. And it was in Woodward’s lab that Katz conducted seminal work on the mechanism of the Diels–Alder reaction,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woodward |first1=R. B. |last2=Katz |first2=Thomas J. |date=1959-01-01 |title=The mechanism of the diels-alder reaction |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0040403901827647 |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |volume=1 |issue=5 |pages=19–21 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(01)82764-7 |issn=0040-4039|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woodward |first1=R. B. |last2=Katz |first2=Thomas J. |date=1959-01-01 |title=The mechanism of the Diels-Alder reaction |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0040-4020%2859%2980072-7 |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=70–89 |doi=10.1016/0040-4020(59)80072-7 |issn=0040-4020|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and by his conceiving of and carrying out a transformation that completed a puzzle, revealed the then unknown structure of the alkaloid [[calycanthine]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woodward |first1=R. B. |last2=Yang |first2=N. C. |last3=Katz |first3=Thomas J. |last4=Clark |first4=V. M. |last5=Harley-Mason |first5=J|last6=Ingleby |first6=R. F. J. |last7=Sheppard |first7=N. |date=1960 |title=The Structure of the Alkaloid and its Degradation Product, Calycanine |journal=Proceedings of the Chemical Society |pages=76–78}}</ref>  Katz was awarded the [[Ph.D.]] degree in 1959 and then moved into a faculty position in chemistry at Columbia University.<ref>[http://www.columbia.edu/cu/chemistry/fac-bios/katz/group/index.html Katz Group Department of Chemistry]</ref>

== Academic career ==
Katz was an instructor at [[Columbia University]] from 1959 until 1961, then an assistant professor from 1961 to 1964. He became an Associate Professor in 1964, and then a full Professor in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-05-18 |title=Chemistry Group |url=http://www.columbia.edu/cu/chemistry/fac-bios/katz/group/index.html |access-date=2022-07-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518045904/http://www.columbia.edu/cu/chemistry/fac-bios/katz/group/index.html |archive-date=2021-05-18 }}</ref> In 1965, he was a Visiting Associate Professor at University of California Berkeley, and he was a Visiting Professor at the University of Konstanz, Germany in 1988.   In 2009, he retired, becoming Professor Emeritus.

== Personal life ==
It was at Columbia that Katz met Meta Oehmsen, a graduate student in English literature, whom he married in 1963.  [[Joshua Katz]], their son, is a linguist and classicist.
